raw.description:
Job Title: Campaign Organizing Strategist

Department: Campaigns

Location: Los Angeles (preferred) or remote in California

This position requires an ability to travel.

Reports To: Campaign Manager

Context: At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 800 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees.

Scope: The Campaign Organizing Strategist is responsible for designing the campaign organizing component of strategic planning in collaboration with the manager and Chapter Director. The Campaign Organizing Strategist supports the planning and coordination of campaigns which win real victories and build the grassroots power to accomplish Sierra Club priorities, which are: to address climate disruption, transform the energy economy, protect communities from pollution, ensure access to the outdoors for all and protect our lands, water and wildlife. The Chapter(s) is a crucial partner for the Campaign Organizing Strategist to successfully carry out strategic plans.

The Campaign Organizing Strategist works closely aligned with volunteers, partners, and staff across states, while harnessing all of the strategic levers of Sierra Club including legal, communications, digital strategies and subject matter/campaign expertise. The Campaign Organizing Strategist coordinates and guides the team of organizers and volunteer teams, ensuring successful implementation of campaign goals, and robust collaboration in alignment with and supported by the manager. The Campaign Organizing Strategist will work with state leadership to develop state based, regional,and local strategies, coordinate implementation plans with the field teams, communicate priorities and track metric benchmarks.

The Campaign Organizing Strategist provides leadership to volunteer and staff organizers in the state(s), fosters volunteer leadership and shapes the leadership ladder, participates to produce educational materials, presentations and reports, research, testifies, lobbies and develops subject matter expertise on relevant topics. The Campaign Organizing Strategist is empowered to represent the Sierra Club to government officials, the media and other organizations, including coalition spaces.

Job activities include but are not limited to:

    1. Campaign Strategy and Implementation: Works closely with the Deputy Director, Chapter Director and Campaign teams to design the creation of state or multi-state strategic planning, and facilitates the organizing strategy, balancing national and state Sierra Club priorities. Works to incorporate key state and chapter stakeholders, including volunteers, to create and implement a campaign of the overarching strategic plan. This includes leading the creation of multi-issue state campaign plans, organizing tactics, conducting or overseeing research, developing engagement strategies, facilitating organizing meetings, volunteer integration, and developing and leveraging partnerships. Tracks policy and regulatory proceedings in the state that are relevant to a specific campaign, identifies opportunities for engagement, mobilization, or intervention. Ensuring that campaigns are rooted in equity and justice and inclusive of frontline and directly impacted communities. May be asked to consult or support on budget, fundraising, and large scale strategic planning.

    2. Campaign Team Leadership. Creates a state (or multi-state) campaign team space to support and coach organizers, track campaign progress, and create a positive team culture with the support and guidance of the manager. Guides team members to develop campaign plans to achieve outcomes in the state. Ensures that organizers have access to resources and uses expertise to support the training team to develop and facilitate training on the craft of organizing and key campaigning skills. Supports organizers to effectively deliver on grassroots campaigns which win real victories and build the grassroots power of Sierra Club. Works with the Campaign team to determine and track metrics and progress towards campaign goals, provides metric guidance and support..

    3. Collaboration. Builds a healthy, mutually accountable relationship with Chapter staff and volunteers to carry out Sierra Club priorities. Communicates clear expectations, capacity, and works in strategic alignment to accomplish Sierra Club’s priority goals. Prioritizes relationships with volunteer leaders and coordinates with other Sierra Club stakeholders as needed.

    4. Volunteer Leadership Development. Support the development of a comprehensive volunteer development strategy to support volunteers from onboarding to leadership through training, coaching, and mentorship. Coordinate with state staff to support volunteer leadership development and organizing metrics. Identify and develop new and existing volunteers to support as they assume new leadership roles and build Sierra Club’s grassroots power and extend outreach into communities. Supports and trains volunteers on organizing skills and developing issue expertise. Develop volunteer leaders who are skillful at facilitating effective, healthy teams.

    5. Strategic Local Representation of Sierra Club. In coordination with state and Chapter staff and volunteers, develop or participate in strategic communication and grasstop engagement strategies and metrics. Represents Sierra Club priorities to public officials, partner organizations, and to the media. Maintains positive relationships with strategic partners, coalitions, members of the media, grassroots leaders, elected officials, and government officials when strategic and aligns with the strategic priorities in the state. As needed, serves as Sierra Club spokesperson to media outlets and promotes volunteer and partner organization media exposure.

    6. Build and Participate on Teams: Build, maintain, and participate on teams to advance state level specific campaign work and Chapter organization building. Develop volunteer leaders who are skillful at facilitating effective, healthy teams.

    Seasonal Activities:

    Heavier seasonal workloads may occur as a result of project deadlines, staff absences and vacancies, and during peak activity periods. Frequent weekend and/or evening work required.

The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:

    • Campaign Leadership: Substantial experience as a field organizer, campaign strategist, and/orleading community organizing campaigns prior experience and/or demonstrated ability in developing, training, and coaching teams.. In-depth knowledge and experience of the craft of grassroots organizing, campaign development and implementation, and power building

    • Strategy Development and Campaign Planning: Substantial experience planning and managing a state or state campaign, including campaign planning, strategy development, integrating multiple strategies and tactics including organizing, policy, lobbying, communications, and working with senior level political and business leaders.

    • Effective Communication: Highly developed communication skills, with a focus on communicating effectively across different groups of stakeholders, internally and externally. Demonstrated ability to communicate complex ideas effectively and develop succinct, compelling calls to action.

      • Team Building: Demonstrated leadership experience leading a team of peers and working within a team structure collaboratively. Ability to build collective vision, trust, and mutual accountability with team members. Experience working closely with volunteers and developing volunteer leaders.

        • Data Practices: Experience using quantitative data (for example, numbers of people engaged) and qualitative data (for instance, stories about people taking action) to inform and evaluate organizing work. Experience building data accountability systems and supporting teams to track and measure the success of organizing tactics.

        • Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate.

        • Uplifting and additive. You see mistakes as opportunities for growth; problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a constructive approach, can-do attitude, a sense of humor, and authentic kindness wherever you go.

The strongest candidates will also demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:

    • Issue Expertise: Knowledge of environmental and energy issues, and either expertise or an ability to develop expertise in state energy, climate justice, and/or conservation areas.

    • Political Expertise: Knowledge of the political, policy, and regulatory landscape in the state. Best candidates will have relationships with some of the major players in business, organizations, and government.

    • Tech Competency: Working knowledge and experience with G-Suite, Zoom, Canva, Mobilize, and Hustle and the ability to learn new technology tools to support organizing and campaign goals. The ability to train and coach staff and volunteers on tools.

    • Demonstrates the ability to create rapport and inspire trust. Open to feedback and the ability to learn new skills.

      • This job description encompasses all of the functions held by this position. A realistic annual work plan will be developed based on the strategic priorities and campaign goals of the state and/or region. The work plan will be approved by this position’s manager and adjusted as needed throughout the year. Depending on the needs of the state and/or region, the (Position Name) may be doing some of these functions more than others. The work plan is the tool a manager will use to ensure there is clarity around expectations and work responsibilities.

To Apply

The Sierra Club provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all staff members. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, lived experience and skills. The Sierra Club does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, immigration status, socioeconomic status, ancestry, age, size, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, familial status, veteran status, disability, AIDS/HIV status, medical condition, prior conviction, arrest history, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The Sierra Club values applicants who are people that identify as Black, Indigenous, and other minoritized groups; women; queer, transgender, gender non-conforming, and gender fluid people.

We value professionals who are proactive, detail-oriented, and dedicated to excellence, and we provide a dynamic and inclusive environment that fosters professional growth and innovation. If you are ready to make a significant impact in the energy sector while advancing your career with a respected global organization, Rimkus invites you to join our team and contribute to projects that shape the future of energy infrastructure.


Responsibilities

  • Lead the structural analysis and design for global energy projects ensuring compliance with industry codes and standards.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams including geotechnical, mechanical, and civil engineers to deliver integrated solutions.
  • Conduct structural assessments and provide expert recommendations for maintenance, rehabilitation, or failure investigations.
  • Develop detailed engineering reports, technical specifications, and construction documentation.
  • Provide mentorship and technical guidance to junior engineers and project staff to enhance team capabilities.
  • Interact with clients and stakeholders to understand project requirements and deliver effective engineering solutions.
  • Stay current with advancements in structural engineering and energy sector technologies to innovate and improve project outcomes.
  • Oversee quality control processes to ensure accuracy and integrity of structural engineering work.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Civil or Structural Engineering from an accredited institution.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license or equivalent certification is highly preferred.
  • Minimum of 15 plus years of experience in structural engineering, with a focus on energy infrastructure projects.
  • Proficient in structural analysis software such as SAP2000, STAAD.Pro, or similar tools.
  • Strong knowledge of international building codes and standards relevant to energy-related structures.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Demonstrated experience in project leadership and team collaboration in a global engineering environment.
  • Effective communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to present complex technical information clearly.

Benefits

Overview of the role

We’re on a mission to modernize insurance, making it simpler, more accessible, and customer-first. The insurance industry is a $1T market that has remained largely untouched by the digital revolution, and PolicyMe is here to change that. As a remote-first, Toronto-based startup with big ambitions, we’re looking for a Home & Auto Insurance Advisor to help us build the future of insurance in Canada and beyond.

As a Home & Auto Insurance Advisor, you’ll be on the front lines helping customers protect their homes and vehicles while delivering a modern, digital-first experience. You’ll focus on sales execution - handling inbound leads, closing business, and providing clear, honest advice that builds long-term trust with our customers. You’ll also collaborate with the rest of the team to refine our sales processes, share insights from customer conversations, and contribute to the continued growth of PolicyMe’s P&C business.

Reports To: Associate Director, Home & Auto

What you'll be doing

    First 6 months

  • Educate prospective customers on Home & Auto insurance options using PolicyMe’s digital platform and your product expertise, breaking down coverage in clear, honest terms so they feel confident moving forward.
  • Manage a high-volume, inbound pipeline of Home & Auto leads, moving them efficiently through the sales funnel and converting qualified opportunities into closed policies via phone, SMS, and email.
  • Use HubSpot to track every touchpoint - calls, emails, follow-ups, and deal stages - so your pipeline is always clean, up to date, and easy to forecast from.
  • Recommend the right coverage based on customer needs using a consultative, customer‑first approach that balances protection, price, and eligibility.
  • Build and refine sales scripts, talk tracks, objection‑handling, workflows, and follow‑up sequences in HubSpot to improve contact rates, appointment show rates, and close rates.
  • Work directly with engineering and product to refine client digital experiences and communicate how our products are performing.
  • Set the tone and standards for how PolicyMe serves P&C customers by delivering a high‑energy, high‑conversion, but always honest and customer‑centric experience on every interaction.
  • Ensure all recommendations and customer interactions are fully compliant with RIBO requirements, carrier guidelines, and internal policies.

    • 6–12 months and beyond

  • Establish yourself as a top‑performing Home & Auto advisor, consistently hitting and exceeding monthly sales and activity targets (contact rate, talk time, conversions etc).
  • Continuously optimize your own sales process by testing new hooks, discovery questions, and follow‑up cadences - and feeding winning approaches back into team playbooks.
  • Contribute to a scalable, repeatable sales playbook for Home & Auto by logging accurate data in HubSpot, surfacing common objections, and helping refine qualification criteria and next‑best actions.
  • Identify and act on bundle and cross‑sell opportunities with Life and Health & Dental, increasing overall premium per household while keeping customer needs and affordability front and center.
  • Help position PolicyMe as Canada’s go‑to digital‑first distributor of personal insurance by delivering an experience that feels modern, simple, and genuinely sales‑driven in the best sense: efficient, helpful, and outcome‑oriented.

What we are looking for

  • A licensed P&C advisor in Ontario (RIBO Level 1 or higher).
  • 3+ years of experience selling personal lines (Home & Auto), ideally in a high‑volume, phone‑based or digital sales environment.
  • A builder mentality - entrepreneurial and adaptable - with a track record of not just working a process but improving it (scripts, sequences, qualification, and follow‑up).
  • A proven track record of exceeding sales targets in a consultative sales environment, with comfort owning a full inbound pipeline from first contact to close.
  • Strong pipeline management and organization skills: you’re comfortable juggling a large volume of leads while maintaining tight follow‑up discipline and clean CRM hygiene.
  • Strong communication skills and a consultative sales style - you can manage objections, explain complex coverage concepts clearly, and make clients feel heard while still driving to a decision.
  • High empathy and discretion, especially when discussing personal and financial details, paired with a clear sense of urgency and ownership over your numbers.
  • Comfort with CRM and workflow tools (HubSpot preferred) and a willingness to lean into data, playbooks, and feedback to continuously improve performance.
  • High ethical standards and a commitment to compliance, confidentiality, and always putting the customer’s best interests first - even while you’re chasing ambitious sales goals.
  • Experience at a digital‑first distributor is an asset.

Why join us:

  • Generous PTO - 20 vacation days
  • A comprehensive benefits plan with premiums paid in full by PolicyMe
  • Investment in your professional development, including an L&D budget, AI tooling budget, performance reviews twice a year and ongoing feedback to ensure you reach your highest potential
  • An extremely high performing, low-ego, remote-first team that is truly disrupting an old industry
  • Option to work from home or our Toronto-based office (bonus: we cover the costs to bring all our employees in-person twice a year for experiential socials!)
  • Access to stock options based on performance
  • Compensation: The total target cash compensation for this role is $80,000–$90,000 CAD, based on experience. We’ll walk through the details together during the interview.

About PolicyMe:

At PolicyMe, we are Canada’s leading digital insurance solution, offering straightforward and affordable financial protection for families from coast to coast. Our product suite includes Life Insurance, Critical Illness Insurance, and Health & Dental Insurance, all tailored to Canadians' evolving needs. We also offer B2B2C solutions, partnering with organizations to provide seamless digital insurance options. Founded by a team of insurance experts and technology entrepreneurs, PolicyMe is committed to making insurance simpler and more accessible. Since our launch in 2018, we have grown exponentially, selling over $10 billion in insurance coverage to Canadians.

We are proud of the team we’ve built and are excited for those that are yet to join us. We operate with a remote-first culture, attracting top talent from across Canada. If you’re looking for a fast-paced, collaborative environment, working alongside incredibly ambitious yet humble humans, we may be the right place for you! To learn more, visit .

Additional Notes:

  • Job Vacancy: This role reflects growth in our team and expanded operational scope. We’re hiring to support increasing demand and continue delivering an exceptional customer experience.
  • Commitment to Equal Opportunity: PolicyMe is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and provide fair consideration regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability.
  • Accessibility Statement: We are committed to providing an accessible hiring experience. If you require accommodations during the application process, please indicate this in the “Additional Information” section of your application.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

About Mood Health

At Mood Health, we are working to make mental health care easier to access.

For many people, reaching out for help is one of the hardest steps they will take. Our mission is to make that first step feel simple, supportive, and welcoming.

Our clinicians provide therapy and psychiatric care through secure telehealth visits. Before a patient ever meets with a provider, they connect with one of our Patient Acquisition Specialists—the person who helps turn interest into action.

This role is more than customer service. It's consultative sales with purpose.

About the Role

We are looking for a Patient Acquisition Specialist to join our growingteam. This is an ideal opportunity for someone with experience in healthcare sales, insurance sales, inside sales, admissions, or other high-performing customer acquisition/support roles.

You'll work with patients who have already expressed interest in receiving care through one of our healthcare partners. Your job is to build trust, understand their needs, answer questions, overcome barriers, and confidently guide them toward scheduling their first appointment.

Success in this role requires someone who enjoys connecting with people, thrives in a fast-paced sales environment, and is motivated by meeting and exceeding performance goals. While this is not cold calling, you should be comfortable managing a pipeline, following up consistently, and helping hesitant individuals move forward.

If you're competitive, goal-oriented, and passionate about helping people while building a career in healthcare sales, we'd love to meet you.

What You'll Do

Convert referrals into scheduled patients

Engage prospective patients who have been referred by our healthcare partners and guide them through the scheduling process from initial outreach to booked appointment.

Build relationships and earn trust

Use a consultative sales approach to understand each patient's needs, answer questions, and provide confidence as they begin their mental health journey.

Manage your sales pipeline

Own a high-volume referral pipeline by consistently following up through phone, text, email, and CRM tools to maximize conversion rates.

Overcome objections

Help prospective patients navigate concerns around insurance, scheduling, treatment options, or uncertainty about seeking care while providing an exceptional patient experience.

Achieve performance goals

Consistently meet or exceed booking, conversion, outreach, and response time goals while maintaining a high-quality patient experience.

Collaborate across teams

Partner with healthcare providers, referral partners, operations, and clinical teams to ensure a seamless patient experience.

Deliver an exceptional experience

Represent Mood Health professionally while creating positive first impressions that build long-term patient relationships.

What We're Looking For

  • Bilingual Spanish required
  • 2+ years of experience in sales/customer support & experience, preferably:
    • Insurance sales
    • Healthcare sales
    • Inside sales
    • High-volume call center sales
    • Customer acquisition
  • Demonstrated success meeting or exceeding sales or conversion goals
  • Comfortable managing a sales pipeline and following up consistently
  • Strong objection handling and relationship-building skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication
  • Highly organized with strong attention to detail
  • Ability to multitask across multiple systems while maintaining quality
  • Experience using CRM platforms such as HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar
  • Familiarity with healthcare, insurance benefits, or behavioral health is a plus
  • HIPAA knowledge or experience working with confidential information preferred
  • Ability to work weekends as needed

What Makes Someone Successful

You will thrive in this role if you:

  • Enjoy helping people make important decisions
  • Are energized by achieving goals and earning performance incentives
  • Take ownership of your pipeline and follow-up process
  • Can balance empathy with confidence
  • Love building relationships over the phone
  • Stay positive and persistent when following up with prospective patients
  • Are coachable and always looking to improve your performance

Why Join Mood Health

Make a meaningful impact

Every appointment you schedule helps someone access life-changing mental health care.

Performance-based earning potential

Competitive base salary with uncapped or meaningful bonus opportunities tied to booking and conversion performance.

Join a growing sales organization

Become part of a high-performing sales team with ongoing coaching, development, and opportunities to advance into leadership or other commercial roles.

Career growth

As Mood continues to expand nationally, you'll have opportunities to grow into senior sales, team lead, training, partnership, or management positions.

$20—$22 USD

raw.description:
Long Wall Company was created in 2024 to accelerate missile defense technology for the U.S. and our allies. We specialize in ballistic missile defense and are developing Cyclops, a low-cost, mass-producible interceptor. We also produce containerized launchers and offer low-cost targets for threat replication. The future of global security depends on defensive technology that redefines cost, magazine depth, and distribution to deter and defend against evolving threats. Join us.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

Mission-Driven Problem Solvers– The problems in missile defense demand ingenuity. We want engineers who approach challenges with curiosity, embrace failure as a learning opportunity, and stay focused on delivering the best solution for the mission.

Total Ownership– We seek engineers who take full responsibility for delivering flight-ready work while recognizing that no one succeeds alone. The best engineers make their teammates better, knowing that complementary skills create force multiplication and drive mission success.

Sr. Project Engineer (SRM), Cyclops

DESCRIPTION

The Project Engineer for the Cyclops Interceptor Program drives the rapid engineering and integration effort that underpins development of Long Wall’s major interceptor system. This role ensures that internal priorities, resources, and schedules remain synchronized with technical baselines, enabling fast, disciplined execution within a private‑investment‑driven development environment complemented by government‑funded testing. For this role, specific focus will be on solid rocket motor (SRM) development, ensuring propulsion engineering activities remain aligned with the Cyclops technical baseline and program priorities.

While the Program Manager handles customer‑facing commitments, the Project Engineer owns the engineering‑centric project flow: coordinating cross‑functional development, maintaining internal schedule fidelity, resolving execution roadblocks, and ensuring technical work stays aligned with project goals, verified requirements, and readiness needs. The project engineer partners closely with chief engineering, responsible engineers, systems engineering, and mission assurance to protect technical integrity while ensuring consistent development velocity.

Work location Note: This role is remote, based out of Huntsville AL. - As Long Wall grows, we anticipate establishing a site in the Huntsville area. If and when a Long Wall site is set up, the person in this role will be expected to transition to full time onsite or hybrid schedule (if outside of commuting distance) based on business needs at that time.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Drive day‑to‑day internal execution of the Cyclops solid rocket motor development, ensuring engineering, integration, and test teams operate with clarity, pace, and alignment.
  • Maintain detailed internal schedules, resource plans, resource constrained critical paths, and cross‑functional work coordination.
  • Manage internal priorities and development flow, ensuring rapid progress while maintaining technical rigor defined by chief engineering and systems engineering.
  • Coordinate closely with the Program Manager to ensure internal execution supports external commitments, contractual milestones, and program reporting.
  • Facilitate technical decision flow by ensuring engineering discussions, trade studies, design changes, and integration plans remain documented, coordinated, and tracked.
  • Work directly with engineering discipline leads to identify and resolve roadblocks, accelerate hardware development, and maintain configuration stability during fast‑paced builds.
  • Support integration and test operations by ensuring engineering artifacts, procedures, and configurations are ready on time and aligned with verification plans.
  • Track and communicate internal risks, schedule drivers, and technical dependencies; support company‑wide risk management led by mission assurance.
  • Maintain alignment with systems engineering’s requirements, architecture, ICDs, and verification flows, ensuring internal schedules accurately reflect technical needs.
  • Support chief engineering by ensuring development activities remain aligned with the technical baseline, and escalate issues that affect reliability, safety, or mission readiness.
  • Help build scalable project management processes, templates, and execution models that will be used for future programs as the company grows.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering or technical discipline, or equivalent experience in complex aerospace or defense development.
  • 8+ years of experience or support of engineering project management, integration leadership, or technical project execution.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Demonstrated experience coordinating engineering teams, managing schedules, and driving technical development cycles.
  • Strong experience with engineering workflow management, development planning, and coordinating cross‑functional technical work.
  • Proven ability to operate effectively in fast‑paced environments that combine private‑investment‑driven development with government test requirements.
  • Ability to interpret engineering artifacts, requirements, and configurations and convert them into actionable schedules and resource plans.
  • Excellent organizational and communication skills; capable of aligning engineering teams, surfacing risks early, and maintaining clarity across disciplines.
  • Demonstrated ability to partner closely with technical authorities (chief engineering, systems engineering, mission assurance) to ensure disciplined technical execution.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience with solid rocket motor development, integration, manufacturing, test and readiness.
  • Experience supporting missile defense, launch vehicle development, aerospace hardware integration, or other technically complex systems.
  • Familiarity with requirements flow‑down, verification planning, ICD management, and configuration control.
  • Prior experience working within a hybrid program environment (internal rapid development + government‑funded test campaigns).
  • Working knowledge of common project management tools for scheduling, risk control, and engineering tracking.
  • Ability to translate ambiguous technical input into structured execution plans.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Ability to sit or stand for extended periods.
  • Ability to use a computer for assignments and communicate effectively in person, via telepresence, and by phone.
  • Ability to travel between Long Wall sites as needed.

ITAR Requirement

This position requires access to information protected under US export control laws, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations and/or the Export Administration Regulations. As such, US person status (including US citizens, U.S. permanent residents, individuals granted U.S. asylum status, or individuals admitted in U.S. refugee status) is a required qualification for this position.

Equal Opportunity Employer

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, genetics, or citizenship status (when otherwise legally authorized to work and access export-controlled data) and will not be discriminated against on the basis of such characteristics or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. We encourage applicants of all ages.

This role is ideal for a detail-oriented, collaborative resourcing professional who thrives in a fast-paced, matrix environment and is passionate about enabling excellent delivery through effective people allocation.

We would welcome someone based near our London or Manchester office but we don't want to limit access to top talent so we are open to remote working for the right person.

Responsibilities

The following are example responsibilities of this position and are, as such, not meant to be exhaustive, nor convey every responsibility that may vary over time, without changing the essence of this position:

  • Day-to-Day Resourcing for the Assigned Business Area: Own the day-to-day staffing of work within the assigned business area, matching people to projects, engagements or initiatives based on skills, availability, experience and development needs. Manage incoming resourcing requests in line with Group standards, including request intake, prioritisation, allocation and confirmation. Maintain an accurate, forward-looking view of demand, capacity and skills, flagging risks and opportunities to the Resourcing Director and local leadership. Apply the Group’s resourcing principles, decision rights and utilisation guardrails to support consistent staffing decisions across legacy and acquired entities. Embed development and career goals into allocation decisions in partnership with People/HR.
  • Resourcing Operating Cadence and Governance: Run the regular resourcing cadence for the assigned business area (e.g. weekly resourcing meetings, look-ahead reviews and pipeline conversations), with clear actions and follow-through. Provide accurate, timely inputs into the Group resourcing cadence chaired by the Resourcing Director, including hot/cold spots, skill gaps, upcoming delivery risks and cross-area redeployment opportunities. Escalate decisions, risks and resource conflicts on a timely basis with clear options and recommendations.
  • Acquisition Integration of Resourcing Activities: Support the integration of acquired-entity resourcing activities into the assigned business area, working under the direction of the Resourcing Director. Help align acquired-entity teams onto Group resourcing processes, tooling, skills taxonomies and data standards, including migration of in-flight projects and people onto Group systems. Build effective working relationships with Resourcing colleagues and Project Leaders from acquired entities, and identify opportunities for cross-entity staffing, redeployment and skills sharing.
  • Data, Systems and Process Discipline: Maintain high data quality in the Group’s Resourcing systems for the assigned business area, including project staffing, allocations, availability, skills and pipeline information. Use professional services automation, capacity and CRM platforms (e.g. Salesforce, Kantata or equivalent) effectively, and champion their consistent use. Drive compliance with resourcing-related processes and identify recurring resourcing frictions, proposing improvements to the Resourcing Director.
  • Reporting and Insight: Produce regular resourcing reporting for the assigned business area, including utilisation, forward capacity, skills mix, time-to-staff and external/independent usage. Provide clear, evidence-based insight to leaders to support staffing, hiring and development decisions. Feed local insights into the Group resourcing performance pack maintained by the Resourcing Director, ensuring a single, consistent source of truth.
  • Independents, Freelancers and Delivery Role Clarity: Manage the use of independent principals and freelancers within the assigned business area, in line with Group onboarding, compliance and quality standards. Co-ordinate freelancer onboarding, allocation and offboarding, working with People/HR, Finance and Procurement as required. Capture end-of-project feedback to inform future resourcing decisions. Help embed Experience Maps, role definitions and RACI expectations within project staffing.
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Collaboration: Build strong, trusted relationships with Project, Account and Functional Leaders within the assigned business area, acting as their day-to-day Resourcing point of contact. Maintain a clear interface with People/HR on recruitment planning, onboarding, development goals and wellbeing considerations. Collaborate with Resourcing Manager peers across other business areas to enable cross-area redeployment, balance workload and share good practice.

About You

The following criteria outline the minimum hiring criteria for this position, unless otherwise stipulated below as “preferred,” or “a plus.”

  • Solid experience in a resourcing, workforce planning, project operations or similar role within a complex, multi-practice or multi-jurisdictional services environment.
  • Demonstrable experience of running a resourcing cadence and balancing demand, capacity and capability for a defined business area.
  • Working knowledge of professional services automation, resource management and CRM platforms (e.g. Salesforce, Kantata, or equivalent), and a track record of using these systems effectively day to day.
  • Experience of supporting integration or harmonisation activities following acquisitions or organisational change is desirable.
  • Knowledge of the management consulting, pharmaceutical services and/or wider life sciences industry is preferred.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to advise and challenge senior business leaders constructively.
  • Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and numerical skills, with the ability to interpret resourcing data and translate it into clear actions.
  • Collaboration: A collaborative, solution-focused approach with high integrity and discretion when handling sensitive people-related information.
  • Project Management, Time Management & Organisation: Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, work to deadlines and operate effectively in a fast-changing environment.
  • Compliance Awareness: Awareness of relevant compliance considerations relating to the engagement of independent contractors and freelancers.

About Prescient Healthcare Group

Prescient Healthcare Group is a specialist pharmaceutical consulting firm, partnering with biopharmaceutical clients to turn science into commercial value. Our practices span Competitive Strategy, Medical, Real World Evidence, VP&A and Commercial, supporting some of the world's leading life sciences organisations.

We are currently in an exciting period of growth and transformation, with a major programme under way to replace and consolidate our core enterprise systems. The Enterprise Systems Manager will play a hands-on role in delivering that programme and in operating the systems that underpin how we work.

We are an equal opportunity employer and fully comply with applicable employment legislation across all geographies in which we operate.

Overview

Flexible Worker Contract 

Location:Remote

About the role

We’re looking for Examiners to join our Assessment Delivery team on a flexible worker contract for the following qualification:

T Level Technical Qualification in Education and Early Years

As an Examiner, you’ll use your subject knowledge to mark external assessments and submit results throughout the summer 2027 marking window, helping to ensure learners receive fair, consistent and accurate results.

If you’re an Early Years or Childcare teacher, lecturer, trainer or assessor, this is a great opportunity to put your expertise to use and make a valuable contribution to the assessment of learners.

Marking window dates are subject to change and will be communicated throughout the process should you be successful.

How you'll make an impact:

  • Following and maintaining the standard set by the Chief Examiner, applying the mark scheme consistently and accurately
  • Reporting suspected malpractice or safeguarding concerns to the Assessment Delivery team
  • Attending examiner standardisation and other meetings as required – standardisation events will be run remotely and scheduled for weekdays between the hours of 9.00am-5.00pm prior to the start of the marking window
  • Maintaining the confidentiality of NCFE assessment materials, learner evidence and learner details, and report any breaches to the Assessment Delivery team 

We'd love to hear from you if you offer the following:  

  • A relevant qualification at Level 3 or above in education and early years or a closely related subject area
  • Current or recent teaching experience at Level 3 or above in an education and early years related subject, or significant recent occupational experience within the sector
  • An understanding of effective quality assurance and assessment processes
  • The ability to work consistently within tight deadlines 
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills

Feeling inspired? Read the full Job Description to find out more.

Why work as a flexible worker for NCFE?

Our flexible workforce provides supportive quality assurance to ensure that learners taking NCFE qualifications are getting the best education possible. If you become a flexible worker with us, you’ll choose how to fit your work around your other personal and professional commitments – making this a great opportunity to make a difference in a way that suits you.

You’ll receive full training and the materials, tools or equipment needed to ensure you’re able to complete your duties in line with NCFE requirements, with the ability to take on flexible worker contract alongside other work, without the need to be registered as self-employed.

All applicants will be expected to adhere to NCFE’s behavioural framework and to uphold our core values.

You can find out more about how our flexible arrangements work, the flexible worker roles we recruit, and frequently asked questions around the application, induction and training process, and your rights and protections by visiting our Flexible worker opportunities page.  

Shape real change with an NCFE career 

Imagine a career where your contributions affect not only what people learn, but the way that learning is developed and delivered.

With over 170 years of education experience our core purpose remains at the heart of the organisation – to promote and advance learning to create a fairer, more inclusive society, making sure no learner is left behind.   

Want to know more? Take a look at our website 

How to apply 

Before applying, please note that we require all candidates to be able to demonstrate proof of Right to Work in the UK.

Ready to join us and shape real change? Apply with your CV and answer the associated application questions.  

Closing Date: Wednesday 2 December 2026

Interview Date: Ongoing

Interview Details: Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. If your application is shortlisted, we’ll contact you to complete a short task.

 Equality, Diversity and Inclusion (EDI) statement 

We're committed to building rich diversity into our workforce at all levels, to ensure that we understand and are representative of the communities and customers we serve.  

We do not discriminate against anyone due to their gender, sexuality, race, age, religion, beliefs, identity, social background, visible or hidden disability, or neurodiversity. Instead, we pride ourselves on our collaborative, vibrant and high-performance culture which embraces everyone, celebrates uniqueness, and enables everyone's voice to be heard.

Job Description

Data centres are one of the fastest-growing, highest-stakes construction sectors in the UK and Europe, and how critical cooling systems are designed and integrated has real consequences for uptime, build speed, and long-term reliability. We're looking for a driven Business Developer to further our growth in this space, embedding Victaulic solutions into the design process from the earliest stages and unlocking pipeline visibility across the region.

Reporting to the UK Business Development Manager and working closely alongside the Business Development team, this is a high-visibility role at the intersection of engineering credibility and commercial strategy. You'll build and maintain relationships with data centre owners and engineers, shaping specification decisions in Victaulic's favour, while keeping commercial sales teams across the UK and Europe closely aligned throughout the project lifecycle.


What You'll Do

  • Identify major data centre projects early and engage planning offices and design teams to position Victaulic solutions from the outset
  • Build relationships with data centre owners and engineers to influence design decisions at the specification stage
  • Build and expand Victaulic's footprint within key accounts, working across every level of the decision-making chain
  • Maintain close, ongoing communication with commercial sales teams across the UK and Europe to ensure alignment from early engagement through to project delivery
  • Keep CRM (Salesforce) records up to date — tracking project stakeholders, timelines, scope, and next steps
  • Coordinate with the UK Business Development Manager and wider Business Development team on national and international project activity
  • Represent Victaulic in industry associations, building your profile and the company's presence in the data centre community

What You Bring

  • A degree in mechanical engineering, or business management, or equivalent technical grounding
  • Hands-on technical knowledge and genuine curiosity about evolving product portfolios, market trends, and standards
  • Existing relationships with Data Center owners and MEP engineers in the data centre market
  • A track record of success in business development, sales, or account management — comfortable managing complex, long-cycle sales and hitting targets
  • Sharp project management, communication, and presentation skills — you're confident representing Victaulic in the room
  • A collaborative, team-first mindset paired with the independence to plan and execute your own weekly, monthly, and annual activity
  • Willingness to travel within the UK and Europe, including occasional evening events

Why Victaulic

Join a global leader in piping technology with a genuine opportunity to shape how one of Europe's most dynamic sectors gets built — backed by a strong brand, real technical innovation, and close collaboration with a specialist regional team.

Events Manager

Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients.

At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

As an Events Manager, you will plan and execute experiences that bring Doximity closer to the clinicians and healthcare organizations we serve. You will:

  • Support Own and plan our twice-yearly Medical Advisory Summits, bringing physicians and Doximity leaders together for thoughtful discussions about clinical needs, product feedback, and the future of care. Lead planning, invitations, programming coordination, travel, vendors, and on-site execution.
  • Manage Doximity’s presence at medical trade shows, including booth experiences, sponsorships, staffing, logistics, and lead capture.
  • Plan corporate events, physician gatherings, and conference-adjacent experiences that build relationships and showcase Doximity’s products.
  • Produce virtual events and activations, including webinars, product demonstrations, and interactive sessions for clinicians.
  • Manage event calendars, budgets, vendors, and timelines; set goals for each event and measure attendance, engagement, and outcomes to improve future programs.

Location: This role is Remote in the United States. Travel to events is required.

What We're Looking For

We're excited to meet candidates who have many of the following qualifications:

  • Experience owning complex, high-touch events from concept through execution, ideally including executive gatherings, advisory boards, or summits.
  • Experience managing trade shows, corporate events, and virtual programs.
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to keep multiple events, deadlines, budgets, and stakeholders on track at once.
  • Confidence working with senior leaders, physicians, speakers, and vendors, with a thoughtful approach to the attendee experience.
  • Experience in healthcare, technology, or professional communities is a plus.

Compensation

The anticipated total compensation for this role is $85,000 - $119,000 depending on factors such as experience, skills, location, and internal equity.

Our total compensation package may include:

  • Base salary
  • Equity (where applicable)
  • Annual bonus or incentive compensation (where applicable)

Specific compensation details will be discussed during the interview process.

Benefits

In addition to competitive compensation, Doximity offers a comprehensive benefits package for full time employees. Some of our offerings include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Flexible paid time off and company holidays
  • Paid parental leave
  • Professional development and learning opportunities
  • Wellness and mental health resources
  • Remote work support and home office stipend (where applicable)

Why You'll Love Working Here

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

  • Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.
  • Work with exceptional teammates. Collaborate with thoughtful, talented colleagues who value curiosity, humility, and continuous learning.
  • Enjoy flexibility and trust. We support flexible ways of working and empower employees with the autonomy to own their work.
  • Grow your career. Take on meaningful challenges, develop new skills, and shape your career through mentorship and professional development.
  • Bring your authentic self. We're committed to fostering an inclusive culture where diverse perspectives are welcomed, respected, and celebrated.

Our Hiring Process & AI Tools

Doximity may use artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled tools throughout the hiring process to help improve the candidate experience and support our recruiting team. These tools may assist with administrative tasks such as scheduling, general communication, interview coordination, note-taking, or summarizing interview feedback. Human recruiters and hiring managers make all hiring decisions. We are committed to using AI responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable laws.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Doximity is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

We provide resources and guidance that makes it easier to live and thrive with T1D. This is more than a moment -- we're empowering a movement for the T1D community. Share your support and help educate and empower individuals facing type 1 diabetes.

Our mission is to improve lives today and tomorrow by accelerating life changing breakthroughs to treat, prevent and ultimately, cure T1D and its complications. Always, we are guided by a single purpose: As we drive towards curing type 1 diabetes, we help make everyday life better for the people who face it.

The National Director, Workplace Giving & Engagement is responsible for driving the national strategy to maximize revenue through employee giving and employer matching gift programs. This strategic leader will serve as the organization’s expert on workplace giving trends, tools, and technologies, and will partner across departments to maximize revenue opportunities. The National Director will oversee forecasting, campaign development, corporate prospecting, and cross-channel activation efforts, ensuring that workplace giving and matching gifts continues to grow as a significant and sustainable source of revenue for Breakthrough T1D.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and lead a national strategy to significantly grow workplace giving and matching gift revenue across all programs and events.
  • Serve as Breakthrough T1D’s subject matter expert on workplace giving and matching gifts programs, trends, and platforms.
  • Establish high-level vendor relationships and oversee platform strategy to ensure alignment with organizational goals.
  • Set annual revenue goals, develop multi-year forecasts, and oversee financial planning and performance tracking for the program.
  • Track and assess national KPIs; use insights to adjust strategy and set financial goals.
  • Lead the development of external-facing matching gift communications, including emails, web content, and platform messaging, to increase donor participation and match conversion.
  • Serve as the primary architect of the national workplace giving and matching gift prospecting strategy, building a pipeline of corporate partners by identifying and engaging employers with strong employee engagement, volunteerism, and workplace giving program potential.
  • Lead the national matching gift strategy, driving employee-level participation by identifying match-eligible donors, increasing awareness of matching gift benefits, and leveraging tools and partnerships to maximize match activation and revenue growth.
  • Collaborate with Global Development teams (e.g., Corporate Partnerships, Peer-to-Peer, Leadership Giving, Direct Response and Signature Events) to embed matching gift strategies into programs.
  • Serve as a strategic advisor to field staff, providing consultative support to identify opportunities and elevate workplace giving and matching gift strategies within local chapters.
  • Create resources, trainings, and tools to support fundraising staff and volunteers in selling and managing the programs.
  • Represent Breakthrough T1D in national Corporate Social Responsibility and workplace giving networks to build visibility and open new doors.
  • Develop and maintain campaign resources and best practices to support chapter and national staff in executing workplace giving strategies.
  • Set the organizational strategy for effective engagement with the Creating Healthier Communities (CHC) Program and Combined Federal Campaign (CFC) payroll deduction. Serve as the liaison to the CHC and CFC and participate on the Charity Leadership Council.
  • Create a coordinated stewardship plan for workplace giving and matched donors across all channels, collaborating with channel leads to inform and implement strategies.
  • Partner with Finance to define rules of engagement for revenue attribution, application tracking, and donor receipting, ensuring alignment and efficiency.

Qualifications

  • College degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 8 years of experience managing campaigns and directly raising 7+ figures annually through workplace giving and fundraising initiatives with Fortune 500 corporations.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including public speaking for small and large audiences, and the ability to craft compelling partner communications and represent Breakthrough T1D with professionalism.
  • High degree of technological proficiency, with Microsoft Office Suite, donor databases (preferably Salesforce), collaboration platforms (SharePoint, Teams, Zoom), and matching gift platforms (Benevity, YourCause, CyberGrants, Double the Donation, Deed preferred).
  • Entrepreneurial and growth mindset with a collaborative approach; comfortable working both independently and within a team.
  • This position requires complex decisions requiring judgement and initiative.
  • Influence and drive alignment across cross-functional stakeholders and field leadership, building buy-in for national strategies and ensuring consistent adoption and execution across teams.
  • Ability to supervise and mentor staff and provide strategic guidance across the program.
  • Oversee training strategy and resources; guide curriculum development.
  • Ability to travel up to 30% for partner engagement, national meetings, and campaign support.
  • Ability to occasionally lift and transport materials up to 15–20 pounds (e.g., event materials, training resources).
  • Flexibility to work occasional evenings or weekends in support of events, campaigns, or key partner engagements.

Target Salary - $125k - $150k

Essential Functions:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this position, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. The employee frequently is required to use hands or fingers, handle or feel objects, tools or controls. The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, sit, reach with hands and arms, climb or balance, and stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl.

The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and infrequently up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this position include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, and the ability to adjust focus.

The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

Benefits:

Breakthrough T1D offers competitive benefits, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 403(b) retirement plan, voluntary benefits, flexible spending and commuter benefit accounts, an employee assistance program (EAP), life and disability insurance, performance-based bonuses, and generous paid time off. Benefits may vary by job level and full time or part time status.

Additional information:

Requests for medical, religious, and other exemptions will be considered on an individual basis. Breakthrough T1D will comply with all federal, state, and local laws.

Breakthrough T1D supports a diverse and inclusive workforce.
Breakthrough T1D is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

You will be the most senior hands-on application security engineer at Cleo, owning both how security is built into our products from design through release and the security posture of the products we ship, both on-premise and SaaS, as our customers experience them. This is a Staff-level individual contributor role with real program ownership: you set the standards, build the guardrails, and work directly with engineers in the code. You report to the CISO and partner daily with Engineering, and our Cloud Security team. You are not a one-person department: security engineers and consulting partners execute under your direction. Your job is to set direction, make the hard technical calls, and build leverage through automation and partners rather than carry every task yourself.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Secure development lifecycle and guardrails

  • Own and mature Cleo’s SSDLC: security requirements, threat modeling, and design reviews for high-risk product changes, APIs, and integrations.
  • Run and tune SAST, SCA, secrets detection, container, and IaC scanning.
  • Build reusable secure patterns, reference implementations, and policy-as-code controls that make the secure path the default path.
  • Own developer security enablement: Security Champions meeting, deliver the engineering security training campaigns, grow a named champion in every squad, and give developers practical remediation guidance, office hours, and self-service security capabilities.

Product vulnerability management

  • Run risk-based triage, remediation, and verification for application and product vulnerabilities, including remediation SLAs, escalation, and exceptions. Reproduce externally reported vulnerabilities against running product instances and validate patches before release.
  • Own the penetration testing program: scope and coordinate third-party engagements, perform targeted testing yourself, and validate findings through retesting.
  • Run our Vulnerability Disclosure Program, including researcher communications and coordinated disclosure.
  • Coordinate the CVE lifecycle for Cleo products and support product-security incident response.
  • Own the application and product-security controls in Cleo's NIST CSF 2.0 program: track maturity, close gaps, and produce the evidence our audits rely on.

Product security

  • Own the security posture of the products Cleo ships, across SaaS and customer-hosted deployment models: secure defaults, authentication and session controls, RBAC and tenant isolation, admin data access, security-relevant configuration, and hardening guidance for customers.
  • Own the Product Security Roadmap: partner with Product Management, the CTO, and Architecture to get security features prioritized and shipped, including SSO/SAML upgrades, the in-app RBAC redesign, endpoint-level access control, and customer-requested controls, and represent security in RTE Sync and Boundary Review.
  • Be the technical owner for customer-facing product security: triage customer vulnerability-scan findings and penetration-test reports against Cleo products, answer security RFIs and enhancement requests, and author customer-facing advisories, security release notes, and hardening documentation.

AI Fluency Competencies

  • Own threat modeling and security review for LLM-enabled product features, AI agents, and AI-assisted development workflows.
  • Build controls and secure patterns for prompt injection, sensitive data exposure, insecure output handling, excessive agency, insecure tool integrations, and AI supply-chain risk.
  • Apply and operationalize the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework across product and engineering.

Prerequisites

  • 6+ years in application security, product security, or secure software engineering, including experience building or maturing an AppSec program across multiple engineering teams.
  • Strong object-oriented developer: Strong proficiency in an object-oriented programming language is required, with Java preferred given Cleo’s core products are Java-based. You should be able to read, debug, and write production-quality code and be comfortable working across languages such as TypeScript, Python, or Go.
  • Deep knowledge of application attack surfaces: authentication, authorization, API security, business-logic flaws, and modern service architectures.
  • Hands-on experience integrating and tuning SAST, SCA, and secrets scanning in GitHub and CI/CD pipelines.
  • Hands-on exploit reproduction and patch validation: you can take a researcher's report of a pre-authentication vulnerability, reproduce it against a running Java web application, confirm the fix, and write up what the researcher and the customer each need to hear.
  • Coordinated disclosure experience with external security researchers and customers, including holding an embargo timeline and driving a CVE to publication.
  • Product security experience on shipped software with an installed base: secure defaults and hardening guidance, customer-facing advisories and security release notes, and turning a customer's scan report or RFI into a fix-or-explain response.
  • Experience running threat modeling, design reviews, and manual security testing, and working directly with developers through remediation.
  • Clear communicator who can turn technical risk into engineering guidance for both developers and executives, and who can hold a release-gating decision with Engineering leadership when the risk warrants it.

Nice to Have

  • Securing LLM applications, AI agents, or AI-assisted development tools.
  • SBOM (CycloneDX/SPDX), VEX, artifact signing, and SLSA.
  • AWS, Kubernetes/EKS, Terraform, Jenkins.
  • Snyk, GitHub Advanced Security, Semgrep, Burp Suite.
  • NIST CSF 2.0, OWASP SAMM/ASVS, NIST SSDF; supporting SOC 2 or ISO 27001 audits.
  • CSSLP, OSWE, GWAPT, AWS Security, or comparable certifications.
  • Enterprise software with both SaaS and customer-hosted deployment models; SSO/SAML, RBAC design, and multi-tenant isolation; MFT/EDI or other B2B integration products.

A few things we have to offer:

  • Compensation: $160,000 to $180,000 + Bonus Opportunity
  • Great Healthcare + Dental + Vision
  • Flexible PTO
  • Culture of support, encouraging Life-Work balance
  • 401k match
  • FSA and HSA options
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Remote work environment
  • Representing a company with 4,000+ clients and a 99% retention rate
  • Accelerated title and salary growth potential
  • A fun and energetic work environment that makes you excited to go to work every day

We use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in certain stages of our recruitment process, such as resume screening and candidate matching. These tools are designed to support fair and consistent evaluations. If you have questions about this process or would like to request an alternative assessment method, please contact us at .

Cleo Communications US, LLC is an equal opportunity/affirmative action employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

raw.description:
Aras is a leader in product lifecycle management (PLM) and digital thread solutions. As one of the fastest growing PLM companies, our technology enables the rapid delivery of flexible solutions built on a powerful digital thread backbone and a low-code development platform.

Our platform and PLM applications connect users in all disciplines to critical product data and processes across the lifecycle and throughout the extended supply chain. The world’s largest manufacturers are leveraging Aras Innovator to manage their complex product lifecycles to improve production timelines, meet and exceed revenue growth targets, and accelerate innovation. We collaborate with companies in some of the most innovative industries, including automotive, industrial/heavy equipment, aerospace and defense, and high-tech electronics.

About the Role

We are looking for a Technical Customer Success Manager to support our EMEA region, combining strong technical acumen with a customer-centric mindset to ensure subscribers achieve long-term value from the Aras Innovator platform. This role bridges the gap between Customer Success and Pre-Sales: you will not only drive adoption, renewals, and expansion, but also act as the technical anchor within your accounts — diagnosing issues, clarifying root causes, and translating complex technical topics into clear guidance for both business and IT stakeholders. You will work cross-functionally with Sales, Professional Services, Support, and Product Management across EMEA to ensure a seamless and technically sound customer experience.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Act as the trusted technical advisor for Aras subscribers across the EMEA region, driving adoption, business outcomes, and long-term value realization of the Aras Innovator platform.
  • Analyze, triage, and help resolve technical issues raised by customers, working closely with Support and Engineering to ensure timely and effective solutions.
  • Conduct technical health checks, architecture reviews, and platform assessments to proactively identify risks before they impact customer satisfaction.
  • Coach subscribers on PLM best practices, configuration approaches, and system optimization.
  • Facilitate and own technical escalations, ensuring the right internal resources are engaged and customers stay on track.
  • Partner with subscribers to understand technical requirements, map them to platform capabilities, and identify expansion opportunities (e.g. additional modules, integrations, use cases).
  • Support renewal and expansion activities by providing technical validation and building confidence in the platform’s ability to meet evolving needs.
  • Build trusted relationships with key technical and business stakeholders and lead regular business/technical reviews to measure progress toward objectives.
  • Develop technical tools, templates, and best practices to help subscribers succeed with Aras Innovator.
  • Work cross-functionally with Sales, Pre-Sales, Professional Services, and Support across the EMEA region to ensure smooth handovers and a consistent customer experience across the lifecycle.

Who You Are

  • A technically curious, customer-focused professional who is equally comfortable in a whiteboard architecture discussion and a business value conversation.
  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting mindset — able to independently investigate technical issues, identify root causes, and communicate solutions clearly.
  • Comfortable engaging with both IT/technical teams and senior business stakeholders, adapting communication style accordingly.
  • Highly accountable, with a strong sense of ownership and a bias for action.
  • Skilled at building trust-based relationships and navigating challenging technical or commercial situations.
  • Able to clearly articulate technical value, adoption strategies, and solution architecture through strong presentation skills.
  • Capable of working independently with minimal supervision while managing multiple accounts and priorities across different countries and cultures.
  • Experienced collaborating across Sales, Pre-Sales, Support, and Professional Services in a fast-paced, SaaS-oriented environment.

What You’ll Need

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a comparable field.
  • 5+ years of experience in a technical customer-facing role (Technical CSM, Pre-Sales/Solutions Engineering, Technical Account Management, or Professional Services) supporting enterprise customers.
  • Solid understanding of PLM processes, master data, and enterprise application landscapes.
  • Hands-on technical experience with web development and enterprise software architecture (e.g. C#, .NET, SQL, GIT) sufficient to understand and discuss integration and configuration topics with IT teams.
  • Experience with PLM software or a closely related enterprise software category.
  • Manufacturing or industrial sector experience is a plus.
  • Understanding of SaaS customer lifecycle management, renewal cycles, and value realization frameworks.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate technical detail into business language and vice versa.
  • Fluency in English required; additional European languages are a strong plus given the regional scope.
  • Willingness to travel up to 20% across the EMEA region.

We were recognized as a leader in The Forrester Wave™: Product Lifecycle Management for Discrete Manufacturers, Q3 2025. Feedback from our community has established Aras as a top ranked PLM vendor in online review services like G2 and Gartner Peer Insights.

With over 700 employees in 11 countries, we’re looking to add to our incredible team. If you’re passionate about helping develop next generation product innovation, we encourage you to apply!
